Samira — thanks, and congrats on the approval. I reviewed the rack sketch: good starting point.

I attached our lightweight inventory CSV (proposed-node-pool-catalog.csv) and the Redwood preflight checklist (redwood-preflight-checklist.xlsx). The CSV is what our on-site engineers consume for node classification (compute, control, logging), NIC pinning, and local NVMe mappings. The checklist includes network ACLs, NTP sources, time sync, and baseline firewall expectations.

Quick answers:
- We strongly prefer a dedicated management VLAN for the control plane and OOB. It reduces blast radius and simplifies BMC access for OS installs. If you must re-use the colo OOB, we'll need explicit ACLs and jump-hosting with key-based auth.
- Minimum per-node NICs: 2x10Gb for data + 1x1Gb management for control; recommend 2x25Gb for GPU-heavy compute.

Next step: can your field team populate the CSV and share it back by EOD Tuesday? Dev and Laura are copied to jump in on sizing and storage encryption policy.

Adding sizing notes and node-pool recommendations for the planner:

- Control plane: 3x nodes (2x16v CPU, 64GB RAM, 2x1Gb management NICs, 2x10Gb data) -- prefer mirrored SSD for etcd.
- Compute (inference): start with a mixed pool: 4x GPU hosts (A100s/80GB or equivalent) and 6x CPU-only workers for batching & pre/post processing. Each GPU host: 8x NVMe slots recommended for local model cache.
- Storage: ephemeral workloads can use local NVMe with periodic backups to the blockstore. For persistent KV/metadata, we recommend a small HA blockstore (3 replicas) on a dedicated storage cluster or SAN with iSCSI (or Ceph RBD if you already run distributed storage).
- Disk/QoS: reserve 10% over-provisioning for local NVMe wear leveling; set eviction thresholds at 75% to avoid OOM/kickouts during fill spikes.

Network specifics:
- Data plane: 2x25Gb redundant leaf uplinks per rack; BGP between leaf and aggregation with route reflectors as needed.
- Management plane: separate VLAN, BMC with ACLs to Redwood bastion IPs (we'll share the list).

I'll also run a quick compatibility check if you can confirm firmware levels for the server BMCs and switch OS versions (Arista EOS / Cumulus / Dell OS10).

- Dev

Couple of additions from the operations and compliance side:

- Encryption: at-rest encryption required for any model artifacts stored on NVMe. If using local NVMe cache, enable dm-crypt with a keyring managed by the site's HSM/KMS; otherwise, deploy a per-node LUKS volume with KMS integration.
- Audit logs: we need remote syslog endpoints (TLS) and a minimal retention policy (90 days) for audit events. Please share your SIEM ingest endpoint.
- CNI: prefer a CNI that supports egress policies and IP pools (Calico or Cilium in policy-mode). We will not support flannel for production private deployments due to lack of advanced network policy features.
- Storage class mapping: map ephemeral NVMe to local-fast storage class; persistent volumes should default to the HA-blockstore class with replication factor 3.

Operational ask: can Havenbrook provide their NTP/chrony server FQDN and a contact for weekly maintenance windows (we suggest Tue 02:00–04:00 local for kernel and OS updates)?

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
